title: Two gaps on a grid
hook: Explore the evidence behind a cosmic question.

knows: Light and gravity help astronomers study the universe.
doesNotKnow: When every separation is multiplied by the same scale factor, a larger initial separation has a larger absolute increase. The proportional change is the same for both gaps.

misconception: A learner may choose: The initially smaller gap
objective: Use the visual model to reason about: In a uniform-expansion model, both gaps grow by the same factor. Which gap gains more absolute distance?

claims.text: Question, correct answer and explanation: In a uniform-expansion model, both gaps grow by the same factor. Which gap gains more absolute distance? The initially larger gap. When every separation is multiplied by the same scale factor, a larger initial separation has a larger absolute increase. The proportional change is the same for both gaps.
Visual caption: Same factor, larger gain. The SVG is a conceptual illustration, not measured data or a scale model.

recall.question: In a uniform-expansion model, both gaps grow by the same factor. Which gap gains more absolute distance?
options: Both gain the same absolute distance
recall.why: When every separation is multiplied by the same scale factor, a larger initial separation has a larger absolute increase. The proportional change is the same for both gaps.
